column1: # DRAGON BALL FighterZ: Arc System Works / Bandai Namco, Unreal Engine 4 (legacy version 4 paks, game folder RED), SDK 4.5.0, NVN, movie module; update 1.33 (v1703936).
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py), brought up on Android
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon (Big Brain Academy: Brain vs. Brain sets a heap only then)
# Android: in battle the game makes and finalizes an 8 MiB shader-code pool every few seconds. File-backed (the default), each placement read it back from flash (2,065 major
# faults, 10-34 ms) and each finalize gave it back on the render thread (8-19 ms): dropped frames at 60 fps. Retroid Pocket Nova, Turnip Gen8 V39, 2026-11-22
# Unreal Engine 4 fills CPU-uncached texture pools and never flushes (OCTOPATH TRAVELER, FINAL FANTASY TACTICS)
# Unreal Engine 4 with legacy version 4 paks keeps every shader inline in the cooked packages (shader_split.py ue_legacy_jobs), as OCTOPATH TRAVELER
# Game settings > Aspect ratio (dm/games/README.md "Aspect ratio without a variant"): the game renders at the picture's shape (dm/host/android/dbfz_aspect.c, patches.py OBS_DBFZ_RES):
# Unreal's r.SetRes width becomes the shape times the height (1920x1440 docked at a taller shape, 2520x1080 at 21:9), so the render targets and the HUD's anchors follow
# the screen. Taller: the cameras keep their horizontal reach and the battle's bottom HUD moves to the bottom edge. Wider: the cameras keep their 16:9 height of view
# (more of the stage at the sides; the walls are the game's own) and the bottom HUD moves out to the side edges; menus keep their centred 16:9 layout, as the other
# wide games here. The character select's camera dollies so its backdrop covers any shape. Any row adds Screen shape (the window's own shape). 16:9 stays the default
